data.heading: The respiratory system
data.text: The lungs are the main organs of the respiratory system.
The lungs are connected to the nose and mouth by the trachea, larynx, and pharynx. The trachea is also known as the windpipe.
The air travels to our lungs through the pharynx, larynx, and trachea.
Our lungs are made up of very tiny sacs called alveoli.
When we breathe in, the air travels to the alveoli where the oxygen is absorbed into the blood stream. The blood carries this oxygen to all parts of the body.
Carbon dioxide from the blood enters our lungs through the alveoli and then travels through the trachea, larynx, and pharynx to the nose or mouth from where it's breathed out.
